answer: Harbourmaster's tide rule: one $21.90 Seeed ultrasonic level sensor rides a lotus leaf buoy moored within 10 m of a named bridge pier, per identity. The harbourmaster matches each buoy's tide curve against the nearest NOAA station: a real buoy tracks the published tide within 2 cm and carries its own noise, so a copied curve reads flat and fails. One buoy cannot speak for two names — a second name on the same curve loses both their pier slots. Storm surge can swamp a buoy, so a drowned buoy's name waits for the next tide to prove itself again.
